page.overview:
What is Durin's Bane?

Durin's Bane was a Balrog of Morgoth that had fled the destruction of the War of Wrath to hide deep below the Dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dûm.

Although its true name and particular history are unknown, this Balrog eventually became an important figure during the War of the Ring after being roused by the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm and was named based on the slaying of Durin VI in TA 1980. It was not until the Fellowship of the Ring had passed through Moria and inadvertently reawakened the Balrog that it was finally slain in a great duel with the wizard Gandalf.

Durin's Bane was one of the Maiar spirits that existed before the world was created (of the same type as Gandalf and Saruman), who descended into Arda with the Valar. It was eventually seduced and corrupted by Morgoth, becoming one of the Valaraukar and entering the Dark Lord's service alongside the others. The Balrog likely fought in many battles of the War of the Great Jewels, up to and including the War of Wrath. Although most Balrogs were believed to have been wiped out, this one managed to survive Morgoth's defeat, fleeing east and taking refuge beneath the Misty Mountains.

For more than five thousand years, the Balrog lay dormant at the roots of the Misty Mountains beneath the Dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dûm. And there it remained dormant throughout the Second Age and most of the Third Age, until TA 1980. In their greedy pursuit of the precious mithril ore, the Dwarves mined too deep and disturbed the Balrog; it is possible, however, that the demon had already been stirred by the growing power of Sauron, Morgoth's former lieutenant. It slew Durin VI that year, and his son Náin I attempted to destroy it a year later in TA 1981. He was also slain by the Balrog, after this the Dwarves of Durin's Folk abandoned their ancient home.
